summary.headline: IZMO Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR109.16 crore (+82.5% YoY), with FY26 revenue up 26.8% to INR284.88 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 posted the highest quarterly revenue in company history at INR109.16 crore, up 82.5% YoY and 84.7% QoQ, with net profit of INR17.3 crore. Management attributed the jump partly to a one-off special project for a client group, where a large share was passed through as outsourced expense, which lifted other expenses to about INR69 crore. FY26 consolidated net profit was INR47.56 crore, broadly flat YoY, which management tied to izmoMicro investment-phase costs. Management guided FY27 izmoMicro revenue to INR45-50 crore, EBITDA margin to 20-25%, and said it is raising about INR150 crore (equity-cum-debt, not yet finalised) mainly for capex.

segments.name: izmoStock (studio/imagery)
segments.commentary: Most established division with steady subscription revenue; completely redesigned portal launched last year is gaining traction with rental, insurance, leasing and dealer customers.

segments.name: izmoCars (automotive digital marketing)
segments.commentary: Completed Stellantis rollout across its European aftersales network; some Q4 revenue came from one-off OEM projects, per management. US organic client additions continued, and Geronimo (UK) added OEM and dealer clients in Germany and Central Europe.

segments.name: FrogData (decision intelligence)
segments.commentary: Products include FDAP, Warranty Boost+, FixedOps Mojo and FixedOps Velocity; gross revenue retention above 93%. Revenue was flat for two quarters, which management attributed to a sluggish market, and it says a resurgence began in Q4; Ford partnership extends to FordDirect's The Shop.

segments.name: izmoMicro (semiconductor packaging and silicon photonics)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR40-60 crore (figures given differ within the call) with pipeline of about INR100 crore; FY27 revenue guided at INR45-50 crore. Capacity about INR150 crore top line today, with expansion to about INR1,200 crore addressable top line. Defence supply contracts and a German subsidiary were added.

guidance_outlook: izmoMicro FY27 revenue guided at INR45-50 crore, against about INR18-19 crore in FY26; management said quarterly timing may be lumpy.
FY27 blended EBITDA margin guided at 20-25%; FY28 blended EBITDA margin guided at around 30%-plus.
Overall FY27 revenue growth expected, but management declined to commit to 30-35%, and said 20-25% is the target.

Capex plan of about INR150 crore in FY27 (about INR125 crore capex, INR25 crore working capital), with expansion targeted to come on stream around mid-FY27 and revenue from Q3 FY28 per management timeline.
Other expenses expected to fall in the next quarter after the one-off project.
capex_capacity: Current silicon photonics/packaging capacity is about INR150 crore top line; the current INR40 crore order book would take about 9 months to execute.
Post-expansion addressable top line about INR1,200 crore; management said it could reach about INR200 crore top line once the expansion is in place.
Phased utilisation plan post-expansion: about 20% for the first 6 months, then 50-60%, then 80-90%.
Expansion targeted by mid-FY28 implementation per management timeline; the project takes about one year to implement.
Funding: about INR300 crore external funding was referenced earlier; management now says INR100-150 crore is being raised, as equity-cum-debt, with a decision expected in 30-45 days.
demand_pricing: Management cited hyperscaler data centre investments in India of over INR3 lakh crore and a global silicon photonics TAM of about $30 billion, expected to reach about $80 billion in a couple of years.
Packaging cost share: 8-10% of chip cost at OSAT level, about 50% for advanced packaging, and about 80% for silicon photonics, per management.
Gross margin on packaging is 50-60%, with silicon photonics higher, per management.
Competition: management said there is no direct competitor in India; globally, the US, Spain and Korean/Taiwanese players are active.
Receivables are about 100-110 days; large clients such as Hertz, Stellantis and Avis pay in 4-5 months, and management said operations remain cash-flow positive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline YoY and is the current margin normalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin dip was a conscious choice to build revenue and client campaigns, and that margins should recover as izmoMicro scales and the cost base stays flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the izmoMicro FY27 revenue and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 izmoMicro revenue guided at INR45-50 crore; order book about INR40 crore with a pipeline of about INR100 crore, though the call also cited INR60 crore earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses jump to INR69 crore and will they persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a special project for a client group led to large outsourced, pass-through expenses; costs should decline next quarter, but a similar pass-through project may recur in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will izmoMicro be funded, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is raising INR100-150 crore, as equity-cum-debt; the route and split are not yet finalised, with an announcement expected within 30-45 days.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly is the order book executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timelines range from 3 months to 2 years depending on the project; the INR40 crore order book would take about 9 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and why the delay in raising it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR150 crore is being raised, with about INR125 crore for capex; the delay was due to firming up technology and machine choices before starting the fundraise in May.

risks_watch: Q4 revenue was boosted by a one-off pass-through project; management said Q4 level is unlikely to be repeated in full, so the Q1 FY27 run rate is key.
Funding for izmoMicro expansion (INR100-150 crore) is not yet finalised; dilution or debt terms and timing remain open.
Other expenses at about INR69 crore need to fall as guided, or margins will stay under pressure.
Several management figures on izmoMicro order book (INR40 crore, INR45 crore, INR60 crore) were inconsistent; clarify in the next disclosure.
Customer-concentration risk: management said several key clients are driving izmoMicro work; US subsidiaries are unaudited (tax filings only), per management.
FrogData revenue was flat for two quarters; recovery needs to be confirmed next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the izmoMicro opportunity, but measured on near-term numbers: management declined to commit to 30-35% FY27 growth, and was evasive on izmoMicro quarterly losses and the technical detail of silicon photonics.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% (declining to commit to 30-35%) and izmoMicro FY27 revenue of INR45-50 crore against ~INR18-19 crore in FY26, backed by a ~INR40-60 crore order book and ~INR100 crore pipeline, but the INR125 crore capex is not yet funded and expansion is not due until mid-FY27 to mid-FY28, so the Q4 jump is partly one-off pass-through revenue.
